seoTitle: How to Connect Gmail to Asana: Easy Integration
metaDescription: Learn how to install the Asana for Gmail add-on in 2026 so you can turn email threads into tasks with due dates and assignees without leaving your inbox.
intro: Turning email requests into trackable work is one of the biggest time-savers project managers ask for, and the Asana for Gmail add-on does exactly that from inside your inbox. This guide covers installing the add-on, connecting your account, and converting an email thread into a fully detailed Asana task.

steps.heading: Install the Asana add-on from Google Workspace Marketplace
steps.body: Open the Google Workspace Marketplace from Gmail and search for the official Asana for Gmail add-on to install it.

steps.heading: Authenticate your Asana account
steps.body: Grant the add-on permission to access your Asana workspace so it can create and update tasks on your behalf.

steps.heading: Open an email and launch the Asana panel
steps.body: Click into any email thread and open the Asana side panel that appears to start capturing task details from that message.

steps.heading: Review the auto-mapped fields
steps.body: The add-on automatically maps the email subject line to the task title and the email body to the task description, so check that the details carried over correctly.

steps.heading: Assign, date, and file the task
steps.body: Set the assignee, due date, and target project directly from the Gmail side panel, then confirm the task appears in your Asana dashboard.

faq.question: Can I attach the original email to the Asana task?
faq.answer: Yes, the add-on lets you attach files from the email thread when creating the task.

faq.question: Does this work with any email, or just specific senders?
faq.answer: It works with any email thread in your Gmail inbox once the add-on is installed and connected.

faq.question: Will replies to the email update the Asana task automatically?
faq.answer: The integration is built around converting the initial email into a task; ongoing replies generally need to be added manually as comments or updates.

faq.question: Is the Gmail add-on free to use?
faq.answer: Installing the add-on itself is free, though creating and managing tasks still depends on your existing Asana plan.
